sections.overview: A long-distance migrant, this plover breeds in Central Asia and winters along coasts across three continents.
sections.identification: It is a ground-feeding member of the plover family Charadriidae.
sections.habitat: It nests on dry, open plains and salt pans, then winters on sheltered beaches, estuaries and tidal flats.
sections.diet: Inland breeders take insects; coastal birds mainly eat molluscs, worms and small crustaceans.
sections.behavior: It migrates in flocks, feeds in small groups and may roost in large gatherings.
sections.reproduction: It lays eggs in a shallow scrape on sand, gravel or similarly bare ground.
sections.ecology: Its annual route links dry inland nesting areas with productive coastal wetlands used for feeding.
sections.conservation: BirdLife lists it as Least Concern but reports a decreasing population and loss of coastal habitat.
